items.text: A claim is made about human psychology. The most convincing evidence would be:

options.B: It's logically derivable from established principles
options.D: It matches your personal observations and experience
options.E: Ancient traditions across cultures agree on it

items.text: A study shows X causes Y. Your experience suggests the opposite. Your grandmother's folk wisdom says something different. A respected expert dismisses the methodology. You should:

options.A: Trust the scientific study—it's the most reliable knowledge source
options.B: Weigh the study heavily but consider the methodological critique
options.C: Carefully weigh all sources of evidence
options.D: Trust lived experience over abstract studies
options.E: Value traditional wisdom that has stood the test of time

items.text: Can intuition reveal truths that rational analysis cannot access?

options.A: No—intuition is just pattern matching that can be made explicit
options.B: Rarely—intuition sometimes detects patterns faster than analysis
options.C: Sometimes—intuition and reason capture different aspects of reality
options.D: Often—intuition accesses knowledge that defies articulation
options.E: Yes—there are genuine ways of knowing beyond rational analysis
